exact_target: For a nearest-neighbor walk on Z^d with d>=2 in an iid uniformly elliptic field of transition rows, does annealed almost-sure transience in a fixed direction ell imply ballisticity in that direction?
conclusion: P_0(liminf_n (X_n dot ell)/n > 0)=1; the 2026 claimed proof states the stronger deterministic vector limit X_n/n -> v with v dot ell>0

primary_historical_source.citation: David Campos and Alejandro F. Ramirez, Ellipticity criteria for ballistic behavior of random walks in random environment, Conjecture 1.1, Probability Theory and Related Fields 160 (2014)
primary_historical_source.quote: Consider a random walk in a uniformly elliptic i.i.d. environment in dimension d>=2, which is transient in direction l. Then it is ballistic in direction l.

intake_source.locator: Drewitz and Ramirez, Selected Topics in Random Walk in Random Environment, Open question 2.20, p. 24
intake_source.quote: Let d >= 2 and the RWRE satisfy (UE) and (IID) and be transient in direction l. Is the walk necessarily ballistic in direction l?
intake_source.historical_result: attempted_unsolved; bounded search 2026-09-07 found no resolution
intake_source.prior_gap: Regeneration time finite almost surely does not establish integrability; prior C0041-A001 could not exclude a heavy tail.

new_primary_claim.citation: OpenAI, Directional transience implies ballisticity, manuscript dated 2026-09-23, Theorem 1.1
new_primary_claim.claim: Theorem 1.1 asserts deterministic positive directional velocity under the exact target assumptions.
new_primary_claim.key_unverified_step: Manuscript estimate (5): for some epsilon in (0,1), P_env(a_N < N^(-epsilon)) decays faster than every power of N; Sections 3-8 purport to prove it.
